clarity.justification: The plan is strongly aligned with the multilingual-representation topic and specifies what is varied and measured, including the “CONVERGENCE DEPTH,” “TRUNCATION GAP,” early exits, and late-layer looping on matched multilingual items. Its numerous non-overlapping criteria—such as “>= 3 layers” supporting H1 versus “< 1 layer” refuting it, and “>= 15 pp” recovery versus “< 5 pp” refuting H4—make the predictions directional and decisively falsifiable. However, the causal early-exit logic is internally unclear: H1 says low-resource languages require greater depth, while Experiment 3 refers to “the shallower effective depth d_lo observed for a low-resource language,” without defining effective depth or explaining why it is shallower; moreover, required depth for an answer that remains wrong beyond the final layer is only right-censored rather than directly observed. Thus an expert could execute most comparisons but would need clarification of the central depth mapping and estimand before treating the early-exit result as a clean test of truncation.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is to “feed the last block's residual stream back through the last k blocks one or more times,” which requires custom handling of residuals and attention state but is an implementable transformer intervention rather than a magic step; the phrase “tuned-lens continuation for the same number of extra passes,” however, is insufficiently defined because a tuned lens is ordinarily a readout rather than a computational continuation. The named models and artifacts—“Llama-3-8B,” “Aya-23-8B,” “Qwen2-7B,” mLAMA/BMLAMA, MGSM, FLORES-200, lang2vec, CC-100, logit/tuned lenses, and forward-layer interventions—exist and are supported by standard transformer and interpretability tooling. Resources are unusually concrete, including “1,000 facts,” “250 problems,” “15+ languages,” three 7–8B models with 28–32 layers, “single A100-80GB,” and “3 seeds,” while random-block, temperature, translation, knowledge-type, and already-converged controls make negative outcomes runnable. The undefined continuation control and ambiguity around mapping low-resource trajectories to an early-exit depth require some custom design work, but they do not prevent the main experiments from being implemented.
